grh_1b43708773c77d85233d.title: Angel Unawarepr Snd At End
paragraphs: Rivers End's council wants the condemned shanties of Paradise Flats torn down, but Dr. Christian refuses to displace the poor families until the town provides decent replacement homes. Contractor Grimshaw dismisses the residents as worthless, singling out the simple-minded but goodhearted Duke Angel as proof that they do not deserve model cottages. When severe flooding comes, Christian and Judy try to cross the river to warn Mayor Hewitt that the bridge has washed out. Their boat carries them to Duke's flooded shanty, where Duke has remained behind with children rather than abandon his home. A floating log destroys the rowboat, leaving them stranded, and the mayor is still approaching the broken bridge. Duke, an exceptional swimmer whom the town has always underestimated, plunges into the icy, debris-filled flood and swims upstream far enough to stop the mayor's automobile, suffering a head injury in the effort. His courage forces Grimshaw and the town to reconsider their contempt. Paradise Flats is replaced by the model cottages Christian had sought, Duke receives a medal as Rivers End's hero, and even after moving into his new house he remains endearingly himself, asking whether he can build a packing-box shanty in the backyard because it would feel more like home.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 14, 1939. It is listed as episode 43 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]], Rosemary De Camp, Joe Hamilton, and William Royal. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_1b49a718294f9a30c695.title: A Matter of Priorities
paragraphs: After her father's funeral, Abby expects to sell the family home and radio station and return quickly to her writing career in Los Angeles. Her plans change when longtime housekeeper Maria disappears and Abby discovers that she is pregnant by station manager John Travis, who had taken advantage of her during the months she cared for Abby's ill father. Looking more closely at the station, Abby also discovers that Travis has been abusing his position and draining value from the business. She fires him, takes the house off the market, and commits herself to Maria, the coming baby, and the station. After helping Maria reconnect with the young man who loves her, Abby realizes that staying home and accepting these new responsibilities is the right priority for her as well.
